reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Bang Bang! at Seapunk, then Fwoosh! at Seapunk, then Kaboom! at Seapunk, then Duck and Cover. This spends all 3 Spark and 2 Energy, deals 25 total damage to Seapunk, and gains 5 Block before the telegraphed 11 damage attack.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered Firework Finale, then Kaboom!, then Duck and Cover. That line also deals 25 total damage and gains 5 Block, but it Exhausts Firework Finale and uses one larger hit instead of Bang Bang! plus Fwoosh!.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the chance to Exhaust Firework Finale and to deal the 18 damage as a single hit. It also leaves 1 Energy unused, though the main alternative did as well. In exchange, it avoids Exhausting Firework Finale and uses the two non-Exhaust Spark cards instead.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. The chosen line already takes the maximum available damage and the available Block without sacrificing damage. A different telegraphed attack would make the Block more or less important, but it would not change the fact that this line is damage-maximal and still affordable. A non-attack intent would not make the Block harmful based on the information given.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
